name: overwhelmed
description: Dismay from not knowing how to respond to too many demands, too much stimulation, or something that seems too large to handle.
perceptions: I cannot process everything that's expected of me in the expected time period.
results: seek ways to manage the load or expectations

guidance.description: You can take specific actions to help you regain a sense of control and reduce stress. It's all about taking small, manageable steps to improve your situation.

variations.name: too many things to do
variations.description: Dismay from not knowing how to respond to too many demands.
perceptions: I cannot process everything that's expected of me in the expected time period.
results: seek ways to manage the load or expectations
examples: being a parent of multiple busy kids

variations.name: too big to handle
variations.description: Dismay from not knowing how to respond to a very large task or piece of news.
perceptions: I don't know how to handle this big thing.

guidance.description: This article describes an approach to finishing small chunks of a big project. It could also be applied when you're stuck trying to figure out what actually to do. Make 'researching' the topic one of the to-do items. For instance, if someone you know got some bad medical news, an early activity might be to learn about their condition.

examples: big project you're not ready for
getting some bad news that requires your response

commentaries.quote: Dealing with the complications of modern life can strain your ability to keep up with it: bills, appointments, home ownership, parenthood, spam, avoiding scams, traffic, making ends meet, relationships. It all adds up. Consider taking one thing at a time.
Being overwhelmed doesn't mean you necessarily want it to all go away. It means that you feel 'in over your head' and might need help, or at least to step back and look at the situation as a whole.
If you can find a path with no obstacles, it probably doesn’t lead anywhere.
Remember, you've survived 100 percent of your worst days.
commentaries.attribution: J. Rose in 'Where Wild Things Grow'

commentaries.quote: Sometimes when you're overwhelmed by a situation - when you're in the darkest of darkness - that's when your priorities are reordered.
